title: Farro Salad with Roasted Vegetables
subtitle: Hearty Italian grain salad with balsamic-roasted vegetables
excerpt: Nutty farro meets sweet roasted courgette, peppers, and cherry tomatoes. A splash of balsamic and fresh basil pulls it all together. Serve warm or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Farro has been grown in Italy since ancient Roman times and remains a staple of Tuscan cooking. This style of warm grain salad is common across central Italy.

recipe.batchNotes: Roast a double batch of vegetables and cook extra farro; store separately and combine to order.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the farro and roast the vegetables up to a day ahead. Combine and dress just before serving.

content.text: Farro absorbs dressing well once warm, so dress it as soon as it comes off the hob for the best flavour.
Tip the courgette, peppers, onion, garlic, and cherry tomatoes into the roasting tin. Drizzle with 3 tablespoons of olive oil. Season well and toss to coat.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until the edges are caramelised and the tomatoes have burst.
Meanwhile, cook the farro in a large saucepan of well-salted boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes until tender but still with a little bite. Drain well.
Squeeze the roasted garlic from its skins. Whisk the garlic with the remaining olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Add the warm farro to the bowl and toss to coat in the dressing.
Fold in the roasted vegetables and the basil. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Scatter the parmesan over and serve.

items.symptom: Farro is still tough after 30 minutes.
items.cause: Farro varies by variety; pearled cooks faster than whole.
items.fix: Keep simmering in 5-minute increments until tender.

items.symptom: Vegetables are steaming rather than roasting.
items.cause: The tin is too small and they are crowded.
items.fix: Spread across two tins and swap shelves halfway.

items.cause: Not enough salt in the cooking water or dressing.
items.fix: Add more lemon juice and season before serving.
